briefdescription.para: Constructs the zero polynomial in the given ring.

detaileddescription.para: Returns a polynomial whose terms have been permuted to be in descending order.

Making the copy is not wasteful, because doing the permutation in-place would be require swapping monomials which is slow if they are large. The returned object is not copy (return value optimization) and using move assignment this code will only create the single copy of a Poly p that is necessary to avoid an in-place operation:

xrefdescription.para: : make a separate TermSorter object that allows the temporary vector to be reused between sorts. This should matter for sorting input ideals where there might be a lot of polynomials to go through.

briefdescription.para: Appends the given term as the last term in the polynomial.
Appends the given term as the last term in the polynomial.
Appends each term in the range r to the end of the polynomial.

detaileddescription.para: Hint that space for the give number of terms is going to be needed. This serves the same purpose as std::vector<>::reserve.
Makes the polynomial monic by multiplying by the multiplicative inverse of leadCoef(). Calling this method is an error if isZero().

briefdescription.para: Returns the coefficient of the leading term.

detaileddescription.para: Returns true if the polynomial is monic. A polynomial is monic if the coefficient of the leading monomial is 1. If you are asking this question about a polynomial, that likely means that you are expecting the polynomial not to be zero. So it is an error to ask if the zero polynomial is monic - you'll get an assert to help pinpoint the error.

briefdescription.para: Returns the monomial of the leading term.
Returns the monomial of the last term.

detaileddescription.para: Returns true if the terms are in descending order. The terms are in descending order when mono(0) >= mono(1) >= ... >= backMono. The coefficient of the terms are not considered in this comparison.
